entries.note: Lab 01 says any logged-in user can read any order id. GET /orders/:id calls orderById with req.params.id at routes/orders.js lines 66-69 and does not pass the session user id.
Lab 01 also names the JSON API. GET /api/v1/orders uses req.query.user_id when it is present at routes/api/v1.js lines 42-43, instead of the id in the token.

The order list passes req.session.userId into the query at routes/orders.js lines 51-52. That is the ownership look-alike beside /orders/:id. The sort argument on the same call is scored separately as injection.
GET /api/v1/me loads db.userById(req.apiUser.id) at routes/api/v1.js lines 29-32. The id comes from the verified token, which is the look-alike beside the user_id query on the orders route.
Lab 03 documents SQL injection in login. login() concatenates username and password into the query string at model/db.js lines 13-14.
Lab 03 documents SQL injection in product search. searchProducts concatenates the term into both ILIKE patterns at model/db.js lines 24-26.
The orders route comment and model/db.js mark the sort column as SQL injection because ORDER BY cannot be a bound parameter. ordersForUserSorted interpolates sort at model/db.js lines 100-101.
Lab 16 documents command injection in the network diagnostics panel. The host from the body is interpolated into a string passed to child_process.exec at routes/extras.js lines 32-33.
Lab 03b documents NoSQL operator injection. POST /api/tags-filter puts req.body.tags into the Mongo filter at routes/shop.js lines 40-41.
The same lab's GET path assigns req.query.origin onto the Mongo query at routes/shop.js lines 57-58.
userById at model/db.js lines 17-18 binds the id with $1. It is the parameterized look-alike directly under the concatenated login query.
POST /api/v1/auth/token binds username and password with $1 and $2 at routes/api/v1.js lines 16-17. That is the safe login query beside the concatenated one in model/db.js.
config.js line 9 falls back to a session-secret literal when SESSION_SECRET is unset. The comment marks that fallback as the training flaw. It is not a live credential.
Lab 07 documents the guessable HMAC secret. config.js line 16 falls back to a JWT secret literal when JWT_SECRET is unset. It is a training value.
config.js line 17 falls back to a Postgres URL that embeds a username and password. That default is a hardcoded database credential.
The login handler writes the submitted password to the log at routes/auth.js line 23. The comment on that line marks the log as the flaw.
config.js line 18 reads MONGO_URL and the fallback URL has no user or password. That is the look-alike beside the Postgres URL on the previous line, which embeds a password.
Lab 02 documents SSRF on the URL fetcher. POST /tools/fetch calls fetch on req.body.url at routes/tools.js lines 21-24 with no host allowlist.

The vault-check handler fetches config.imdsUrl and config.vaultUrl at routes/tools.js lines 56-59. Those hosts are configuration, not the request. The comment above the fetches says the host is user-influenced; the pinned statements are not, so this row is the safe look-alike.
